items.title: Far-right AfD leads polls ahead of crucial Saxony-Anhalt state election in Germany | DW News
items.author: DW News
items.content:
<article>It’s the final day of campaigning ahead of a crucial state election in Germany that could give the far right a mandate to govern for the first time. Germany’s far-right Alternative for Germany is heading into Sunday’s Saxony-Anhalt election with a strong lead in the polls, even though authorities have designated the party’s state branch as anti-constitutional and a far-right extremist group. Rival parties have ruled out working with the AfD, while nearly a third of voters remain undecided.

items.title: Why opposition to AI data centers is growing in the US | DW Reporter
items.author: DW News
items.content:
<article>The artificial intelligence boom is creating demand for computing power. Data centers are springing up across the U.S.— and opposition is growing.  
Many U.S. residents say their health problems are being caused by new data centers being built in their neighborhoods. But President Trump only sees the potential economic benefits of these large-scale projects. Not all elected officials agree with him, including Democratic House Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, who is sounding the alarm on the environmental impact — and she's not the only one. This debate is having a significant effect on the upcoming US midterm elections, deepening the divide between supporters and opponents. There is no doubt that the AI boom will change the US, but at what cost? A report by Ines Pohl.

items.title: How Trump’s Gaza plans could strip Palestinians of their property rights | DW News
items.author: DW News
items.content:
<article>Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir has unveiled a plan that would see all of Gaza's population emigrating, following comments by Defense Minister Israel Katz that there was “no real solution for Gaza in the end without this migration” and that the government was “organized and prepared to get them [Palestinians in Gaza] out by sea, by air, by every way possible." Katz said explicitly that Israel was seeking support from US President Donald Trump for the mass emigration plan.  

Since January 2026, the US-led Board of Peace has reportedly been working on plans to rebuild the enclave from the ground up — albeit without announcing how exactly it will do that, and what becomes of Palestinians’ private property and their rights of ownership. Amid various leaks of the Board’s plans, the UN and multiple rights organizations repeatedly issued concerns of possible ethnic cleansing, which is illegal under international law.   

DW asked human rights experts about the legality of the plans — and spoke to landowners in Gaza, who say they simply want to stay on their land and have their right to self-determination respected.
